claim: Thiazolidinediones ameliorate aged-related tissue function decline.

claim: Female mice harbor higher circulating adiponectin levels compared to male mice.

claim: Female mice live longer compared to male mice.

claim: Serum adiponectin was absent in APN-KO mice.

claim: Circulating adiponectin levels were increased by 50% in ΔGly mice.
source: For ΔGly mice, circulating adiponectin levels were increased by 50% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).

claim: APN-KO mice have a statistically significant shortened lifespan compared to WT control on normal chow diet.

claim: APN-KO mice have a statistically significant shortened lifespan compared to WT control on high-fat diet.
source: The survival curves for APN-KO reveal a statistically significant shortened lifespan compared to WT control both in the NCD cohort (Figure 1A) and in the HFD cohort (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the Kaplan-Meier survival curves in Figure 1B with p=0.0002.

claim: Loss of adiponectin in mice accelerates the aging process and shortens lifespan.
source: Thus, loss of adiponectin in mice accelerates the aging process and shortens lifespan.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the lifespan data presented in Figure 1.

claim: APN-KO mice did not show any striking difference in body weight at middle and advanced age on NCD.
source: Compared to WT mice, APN-KO mice did not show any striking difference in body weight at middle and advanced age, both on NCD and HFD (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is shown in the body weight measurements in Figure 2A.

claim: APN-KO mice did not show any striking difference in body weight at middle and advanced age on HFD.
source: Compared to WT mice, APN-KO mice did not show any striking difference in body weight at middle and advanced age, both on NCD and HFD (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is shown in the body weight measurements in Figure 2B.

claim: APN-KO mice exhibit a slight reduction in fat mass at advanced age.
source: However, APN-KO mice exhibit a slight reduction in fat mass at advanced age (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown in the body composition analysis in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The reduction of fat mass in APN-KO mice seems to be due mainly to the loss of subcutaneous fat.
source: The reduction of fat mass seems to be due mainly to the loss of subcutaneous fat (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the fat depot weight measurements shown in the figure.

claim: Adiponectin-deficient mice have increased bone content during HFD feeding.

claim: Adiponectin-deficient mice have higher bone mineral density during HFD feeding.

claim: Differences in glucose tolerance were marginal in APN-KO mice fed standard NCD.
source: In accordance with previous metabolic studies of young APN-KO mice, differences in glucose tolerance were marginal in mice fed standard NCD (Figure 2C).

claim: APN-KO mice fed HFD exhibited significantly higher glucose excursions during an oral glucose tolerance test.
source: APN-KO mice fed HFD, in contrast, exhibited significantly higher glucose excursions during an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) (Figure 2D) reflecting impaired glucose tolerance.
evidence: This is shown in the OGTT results in Figure 2D with statistical significance indicated.

claim: No significant difference in plasma insulin level was observed during the OGTT at the different time points in aged APN-KO mice on HFD.
source: However, no significant difference in plasma insulin level was observed during the OGTT at the different time points (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is shown in the insulin measurements during OGTT in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: APN-KO mice are more susceptible to diet-induced glucose intolerance.
source: This indicates that APN-KO mice are more susceptible to diet-induced glucose intolerance.
evidence: This is an inference based on the OGTT results comparing NCD and HFD-fed APN-KO mice.

claim: Triacylglycerol levels in both NCD- and HFD-fed APN-KO mice peaked at higher levels during TG clearance test.
source: Triacylglycerol levels in both NCD- and HFD-fed APN-KO mice peaked at higher levels and showed a slower clearance of lipids from plasma (Figure 2E and F).

claim: NCD- and HFD-fed APN-KO mice showed a slower clearance of lipids from plasma.
source: Triacylglycerol levels in both NCD- and HFD-fed APN-KO mice peaked at higher levels and showed a slower clearance of lipids from plasma (Figure 2E and F).

claim: APN-KO and WT mice consume comparable amounts of diet.

evidence: This is shown in the food intake measurements in Figure 2G.

claim: APN-KO mice had a significantly higher respiratory exchange ratio.
source: Furthermore, although APN-KO and WT mice consume comparable amounts of diet (Figure 2G), indirect calorimetric studies show that APN-KO mice had a significantly higher respiratory exchange ratio (Figure 2H), indicative of carbohydrate being a more predominant fuel source in the absence of adiponectin.
evidence: This is shown in the metabolic cage analysis in Figure 2H with statistical significance indicated.

claim: A higher respiratory exchange ratio in APN-KO mice is indicative of carbohydrate being a more predominant fuel source in the absence of adiponectin.
source: Furthermore, although APN-KO and WT mice consume comparable amounts of diet (Figure 2G), indirect calorimetric studies show that APN-KO mice had a significantly higher respiratory exchange ratio (Figure 2H), indicative of carbohydrate being a more predominant fuel source in the absence of adiponectin.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RER data based on established metabolic knowledge.

claim: Adiponectin is necessary to maintain proper lipid homeostasis.

claim: Lack of adiponectin prompts glucose metabolism to be more prevalent.
source: Lack of adiponectin prompts glucose metabolism to be more prevalent.

claim: In aging adipose tissue, expansion of B cells in fat-associated lymphoid clusters occurs.

claim: In aging adipose tissue, enrichment of senescent-like pro-inflammatory macrophages occurs.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Camell et al., 2017; Lumeng et al., 2011; Tchkonia et al., 2010.

claim: In aging adipose tissue, loss of tissue protective macrophage subsets occurs that drive inflammaging and compromise glucose and lipid metabolism.

claim: In the liver and kidney, dysfunction during aging is usually apparent as overexpression of extracellular matrix protein constituents, such as collagen and the resulting increased fibrosis.
source: In the liver and kidney, dysfunction is usually apparent as overexpression of extracellular matrix (ECM) protein constituents, such as collagen and the resulting increased fibrosis (Kim et al., 2016).

claim: APN-KO mice did not show significant morphological differences in adipocytes in both young and aged mice compared to WT mice.
source: Compared to WT mice, APN-KO mice did not show significant morphological differences in adipocytes in both young and aged mice.

claim: The epididymal fat of APN-KO mice fed either HFD or NCD show increased pro-inflammatory-like macrophages in the aged mice.
source: However, the epididymal fat of APN-KO mice fed either HFD or NCD show increased pro-inflammatory-like macrophages in the aged mice, as demonstrated by a prominent signal for the macrophage marker Mac2 (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is shown by Mac2 immunohistochemical staining in Figure 3B.

claim: The expression levels of inflammatory markers were drastically increased in gonadal white adipose tissue of APN-KO mice, both on NCD and on HFD.
source: Consistent with the immunohistochemical staining, the expression levels of inflammatory markers were drastically increased in gonadal white adipose tissue of APN-KO mice, both on NCD and on HFD (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR analysis in Figure 4A.

claim: The loss of adiponectin accelerates adipose tissue inflammation.
source: This demonstrates that the loss of adiponectin accelerates adipose tissue inflammation, a characteristic marker of the increased aging process.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Mac2 staining and inflammatory marker expression data.

claim: Aged APN-KO mice on HFD show severe interstitial and periglomerular fibrosis in the kidney.
source: Morphologically, APN-KO mice fed either the HFD or the NCD show more severe interstitial and periglomerular fibrosis.
evidence: This is shown by trichrome staining in Figure 3C.

claim: The glomeruli in aged APN-KO mice have collapsed tufts, accompanied by hypertrophic Bowman's capsules.
source: Compared to aged WT mice, the glomeruli in aged APN-KO mice have collapsed tufts, accompanied by hypertrophic Bowman's capsules (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is shown by histological examination in Figure 3C.

claim: Aged APN-KO mice exhibited a significant increase in kidney weight as compared with aged WT mice.

claim: Mac2 positive intraglomerular signal is significantly increased in old APN-KO mice fed the HFD.
source: Immunohistochemical staining with Mac2 antibodies reveals a significant increase in Mac2 positive intraglomerular signal in the old mice which is vastly more abundant in the APN-KO mice fed the HFD (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is shown by Mac2 immunohistochemical staining in Figure 3D.

claim: The expression levels of inflammation markers were dramatically increased in kidneys of adiponectin-deficient mice.

Across the board, the expression levels of inflammation markers were dramatically increased in adiponectin-deficient mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR analysis in Figure 4B.

claim: Hypoadiponectinemia predicts liver fibrosis.

claim: Hypoadiponectinemia accelerates hepatic tumor formation.

claim: No enhanced lipid droplet accumulation was found in the livers of APN-KO mice compared to WT mice upon short-term and long-term exposure to HFD treatment.

claim: Many inflammatory infiltrates were found in the livers of APN-KO mice on HFD diet.

claim: The expression of inflammatory markers is significantly increased in aged APN-KO mice fed on NCD.

claim: Corticosteroids were upregulated in APN-KO mice compared to control mice, presumably as a compensatory response.

claim: The total number of macrophages in APN-KO mice is doubled compared to WT mice.

claim: Kupffer cells increased in APN-KO mice compared to WT mice.

claim: Monocyte-derived macrophages increased in APN-KO mice compared to WT mice.

claim: Kupffer cells are the major source of the inflammatory response in APN-KO mice.

claim: Increased hepatic fibrosis was observed in old APN-KO mice on NCD.
